title: Aslam Khan Reframes the Defeat and Sends Subeg Singh

blocks.text: Aslam Khan reacts to the Khalsa victory with mixed feelings: he mourns the Mughal losses, yet he is relieved that the Delhi revenue force has been destroyed before it could arrest him for failing to meet imperial demands. The blow that ruined others gives him breathing room, and he immediately begins calculating how to turn the crisis to his own advantage.

In the letter he sends onward, Aslam Khan suppresses the humiliating parts of the story and instead describes the Khalsa as a grave and growing threat. He argues that the power once associated with Banda Singh has not ended but has increased, and he presents the danger in terms designed to move Delhi without exposing his own weakness.

From that calculation he turns toward conciliation as strategy rather than surrender. He drafts terms meant to flatter the Singhs, proposes to use soft promises before force, and calls for Subeg Singh to carry the proposal so talks can begin with the Khalsa.
